decisions.reason: Pluperfect “we’d had” matches 나눴었다; “this conversation” is a natural lead-in to the quoted exchange.
SOL drops 이제 (“now”) from 이제 한 가족 같다.
BASE weakens 터져 나온다 as “kept going off”; SOL loses progressive 웃고 있었다 and replaces 길쭉한 with “tall, slender.”
decisions.replacement: On the screen, a handsome man with a lanky build was smiling brightly. Dozens of cameras and a huge crowd reacted to his every move. Flashes and screams erupted without pause.

decisions.reason: “How old was he again?” matches 몇 살이랬지 better than assuming someone had just said his age.
“Between the two” makes 그 격차 point back to earners vs non-earners without adding meaning.
Spoken “Wait a little longer and…” is punchier while still matching 기다리면.
SOL’s “Maybe” weakens 가능할 테니까, which is teasingly sure, not tentative.
“While” versus “as” is indistinguishable for 낄낄거리며 놀리던.
“What kind of face” is the idiomatic 표정을 짓다; “I wonder” renders 을까.
“Surged along with me” matches 우르르 움직인다; “swarmed after” adds pursuit.
Keeps the fragment beat of 사람들의 주목 instead of merging it into one sentence.
Preserves 순간이었다; SOL’s “for the first time” is not in the Korean.
“Smiled and waved” and dropping dummy “they” are cleaner without losing 웃음과 함께 손을 흔들자.
Honorific singular 계십니다 fits Jin Wikyung, the only person waiting in the hall.
“Looked” is 바라보던; “regarded” is a needless Latinate lift.
“No longer the person” and “threw open the door” keep the then/now parallel in more idiomatic English.
“Chairs scattered along either side” is the more natural word order for 양옆으로 흐트러진 의자.
왔느냐 is a question; SOL turns it into a statement.
“Alone” is the tighter rendering of 오직 그 혼자뿐.
SOL drops hearsay 있다는구나 and replaces frantic 닥치는 대로 with “every force.”
“Battles piled up” is 전투가 모여; SOL flattens that and intensifies 사기를 잃은.
“All our forces” and “before it can join” are natural intercept phrasing for 전 병력 / 합류하기 전에.
“When is that?” keeps 그게; SOL’s “When?” is too clipped.
“Filthy fast” is a calque of 더럽게; “fucking fast” is the natural vulgar intensifier.
Keeps the anxious rhetorical 아니라면?; SOL turns it into a flat conditional.
“A great deal” matches spoken 크게; “considerably” is too formal for this dialogue.
움직여다오 is an imperative; SOL adds “I want you to.”
Subject is the Five Gates’ 인연 with 본가, so “our family” as the other party is closer.
“Without another thought” is the natural idiom for 더 생각할 것 없이.
“Saying” matches 다는 메시지; “announcing” lifts the register.
“I lose Fame” is more immediate first-person for 거절 시 명성 하락.
“Sense of relief” is the natural collocation for 안도감.
게임 중독이라며 is calling himself an addict, not “becoming” one.
SOL drops 보이지 않는 and the shadow 드리워져 over his face.
SOL’s “entire” over-specifies 한 지방.
“Sudden thought” preserves 문득, which BASE omits.
궁금한 게 is curiosity, not “wanted to ask.”
“Go ahead” is the natural prompt for 말해 보거라; “Ask” is too clipped.
SOL drops 도무지 (“at all”) and recasts the confusion as “what I meant.”
“Wanted your advice” is tighter spoken English for 조언을 좀 구하려고요.
맞닥트린 is “run into,” not merely “standing before.”
Keeps the doubled 그냥 stammer that SOL collapses.
“Didn’t open his mouth” is the physical 입을 열리지 않았다 before he uses the tea.
믿을 신 glosses the verb “believe,” not the noun “belief.”
얼굴을 확인한 is checking his face, not “seeing my expression.”
“Pie in the sky” is the idiom for 뜬구름 잡는 소리; “airy nonsense” is generic.
어지럽게 만들었다 is “made me dizzy,” not merely “felt dizzy.”
믿고 있었지 is past progressive “been believing.”
“More than anything else” and plural “facts” are natural for 가장 큰 도움 / 사실만을.
“Thought of myself” versus “considered myself” is indistinguishable for 생각했던.
꺾었다 is “defeated,” distinct from 쓰러트렸고 “taken down.”
여전히 is “still,” not the more literary “had remained.”
얼이 빠진 얼굴 is vacant/“out of it,” not specifically “stunned.”
Splitting the self-correction gives 아니, 였었다 its own beat.
The isolated “No. I *had been*” matches the Korean correction.
Keeps the System pairing “Sinews and Bones” for 근골 rather than a reordered generic list.
SOL drops 물었다 (“asked”) and invents “stared at us.”
SOL adds “badly”/“suddenly” and possessive “my” not in 막혔던 콧구멍이 뻥 뚫린.
시선이 모인다 is gazes gathering, not heads turning.
있는 법이다 is gnomic present; past tense breaks the proverb.
“Dressed in” is a small naturalization of 복색의 without changing the image.
“One of them” is 한 사람과; “one of theirs” is the wrong pronoun.
“My own” clarifies that the reflexive 포권 is Taekyung’s.
열정적으로 is enthusiastically; BASE “hard” and SOL “vigorously” both miss the ardor.
Singular agreement for 지원군이다; BASE mixes “he” with “their.”
“Merely an honor to be included in … tales” matches 낄 / 따름 / 무용담; SOL singularizes and shifts “merely.”
“Freely giving” is 아낌없이 주는; SOL’s “ever-giving” and “warmest” intensify.
Present “I’ve” fits the current thought; “piled up” keeps 모였다, which SOL’s “built up” weakens.
decisions.replacement: *Still, I’ve piled up quite a bit.*

decisions.reason: “Fifty points” reflects 수치; “spent the next two days grinding” fixes awkward “grinded.”
볼일 is business to take care of, not “somewhere to be.”
목적지는 정해져 있었다 is a decided destination, not merely “in mind.”
SOL’s “face fell” and “hung above it” add unstated physical detail to 실망하는 / 현판이 걸린.
Keeps 그리고 (“And”) introducing the plaque.
Same footnote facts in clearer English, still distinguishing 問 from 門.
